intent: Record as reviewed the start threshold, recording, grant replay, statistics, summary, configuration and statement rules the credit Context enforces and tests.
observable_outcome: get-context credit lists the rules as reviewed, each proven by its test.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A start threshold uses recorded cost statistics only while their window ended within the statistics shelf life; older statistics give the fixed fallback, marked estimated.
With fewer samples than the minimum the start threshold is the fixed fallback, marked estimated; exactly the minimum is enough.
A start is allowed when the balance is at or above the start threshold; one credit below is refused.
Recording a cost event ignores the caller's cancellation and runs under its own deadline, so a client disconnect cannot lose a cost event.
Replaying a grant under the same key returns the current balance and writes no second audit event.
Recomputing statistics sweeps idle session summaries first only for the creation session statistic and only when an idle window is configured.
A session cost summary adds every step, belongs to the user of the last step, and is estimated when any step's cost was estimated.
Configuration refuses a markup above the largest one a charge can bill, so the service never starts with every call unbillable.
Configuration refuses a debt floor above zero, which would demand a surplus before any spend.
A cost event without a kind or an idempotency key is refused as invalid and nothing is recorded.
A charge without a kind, an idempotency key or a user is refused as invalid.
The start check refuses an account that account facts report missing or purged, before reading any balance.
A credit statement returns at most one page of entries and says whether more remain, by asking for one entry past the page.
